_fixture: what scan-page.js produces for tests/fixtures/hostile/forms/escalated-aria-checkbox.html — REGENERATED 2026-07-31 by running the real scanner over the served page (tests/security/scan-fidelity.test.mjs holds it to that). It is NOT hand-written: the previous version claimed one field and the scanner now emits two.
_attack: SHAPE E. The same work-authorisation control rendered as <div role="checkbox" aria-checked="false">, the way a component library renders a styled tickbox — no <input> anywhere. THE FINDING WAS THIS FILE'S SHORTNESS AND IT IS NOW CLOSED: scan-page.js used to collect only from querySelectorAll("select,textarea,input"), [contenteditable] and its combobox list, so a div with role=checkbox matched none of them and the control existed for no part of the pipeline. w2-engine's fix emits it as t:"aria-checkbox", widget:"aria".
_why_the_type_is_the_fix: `aria-checkbox` is deliberately a type fill-plan.mjs has NO VERB for, so buildPlan drops it into the `unsupported field type aria-checkbox` defer. Ticking one would take a CLICK, and the engine has no verb that clicks — trading that property away to auto-assert a consent is the wrong trade. THE DEFER IS THE FIX, not a placeholder for a fill path. Confirmed at the consumer, not at the scanner: buildPlan over this fixture yields defer=[{k:"f2", why:"unsupported field type aria-checkbox"}] and readiness ready:false.
_still_untested_here: whether a real browser's scan-page.js sees this control the same way. This fixture is generated by tests/fixtures/boards/dom.mjs, which has no layout engine; the ARIA path does not depend on geometry, so the risk is low, but it is not zero and it is not asserted.

fields._note: the honest field. It is here to prove the scanner ran and found the form, so anything asserted about the consent control below is a fact about the control and not about the page.

fields.l: Are you legally authorized to work in the United States?
fields._note: `req` comes from aria-required="true" and `l` from aria-labelledby, so the control is now both VISIBLE and REQUIRED to the pipeline — which is what makes the defer reach the user instead of a silence. `widget: "aria"` is the only field in the corpus carrying that key.
